Babcock University has confirmed that a student involved in a viral incident at one of its hostels is alive and responding to treatment at the university’s teaching hospital. The institution made this known in a Monday statement signed by its Associate Vice-President, Communication, Media and Branding, Johnson B. Akintayo, following reports suggesting that the student had died. The university said the incident was brought under control through the prompt intervention of the student’s roommates, whose actions prevented what could have been a more tragic outcome. “Contrary to reports suggesting that the student may have died, we wish to assure the public that he is responding positively to treatment and is receiving the necessary medical care,” the statement said. It added that the student and one of his rescuers sustained injuries during the incident and were immediately taken for medical attention. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The incident, which occurred on November 8, 2026, involved a 400-level student and attracted attention after videos showing the student near a window ledge at a hostel circulated on social media. Soyombo essay contest offers undergraduates N900,000 prizes VIDEO: Foreigner buys sea turtle in Lagos, returns it to sea Police debunk viral video of officers’ arrest in Kogi The footage showed some of his roommates attempting to restrain and pull him away from the ledge. The university said it had commenced an investigation to establish the immediate and underlying circumstances surrounding the incident. “This process will help us understand what happened, identify any factors that may have contributed to the situation, and determine appropriate measures to prevent a recurrence,” it said. It urged members of the public and media organisations to refrain from circulating unverified information or attributing causes to the incident while investigations were ongoing. The institution also said it was committed to supporting the student’s recovery and would provide appropriate guidance and other necessary assistance. “We particularly acknowledge and commend the courage and prompt action of his roommates who came to his rescue. We appeal for sensitivity and restraint in discussing this incident, particularly out of respect for the student and his family at this difficult time,” the statement added. The university reiterated its commitment to the safety, health and welfare of its students and employees.
